knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Slope of the Tangent to a Parametric Curve at a Given Point

question.:question/problem:
For the parametric curve 

$$
x=e^{\frac{5}{t}},\,y=\frac{1}{\sqrt{t^{2} + 1}},\,0<t<\infty,
$$

calculate the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=4.$ Do not round the answer.

$m=$
{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
x'(t)=- \frac{5 e^{\frac{5}{t}}}{t^{2}},\,y'(t)=- \frac{t}{\left(t^{2} + 1\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}.
$$

 

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\left(- \frac{t}{\left(t^{2} + 1\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}\right)}{\left(- \frac{5 e^{\frac{5}{t}}}{t^{2}}\right)} \\  & =\frac{t^{3} e^{- \frac{5}{t}}}{5 \left(t^{2} + 1\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, when $t=4,$ the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}m=\frac{dy}{dx}\,{|}_{t=4} & =\frac{\left(4\right)^{3} e^{- \frac{5}{\left(4\right)}}}{5 \left(\left(4\right)^{2} + 1\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}} \\  & =\frac{64}{85 \sqrt{17} e^{\frac{5}{4}}} \\  & =\frac{64 \sqrt{17}}{1445 e^{\frac{5}{4}}}.\end{aligned}
$$
